assumptions: Assay sensitivity: immuno-capture and particle-count instrumentation are sufficiently sensitive to detect orthogonal intact-EV signatures in short-interval lavage/CSF/tissue samples.
Spike-in validity: an exogenous, orthogonally labeled intact-EV spike-in is available and behaves as an internal recovery control without altering biological readouts.
Feasibility: short-interval tissue harvest and single-cell processing are operationally feasible within the chosen animal model and institutional/ethical approvals.
biological_rationale: Rodent intranasal studies report functional effects but lack orthogonal intact-EV exposure linkage (ev-zhuang-2011-intranasal-exosome; ev-kodali-2017-status-epilepticus; ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi). MISEV2023 emphasizes membrane-protection and orthogonal controls to attribute activity to intact EVs (ev-misev2023-quality-framework). A spike-in–controlled in vivo→ex vivo bridge with a single-cell transcriptional readout in tissue-resident microglia provides a higher-dimensional, mechanism-relevant discrimination between membrane-protected EV-associated effects and soluble/secretome artifacts; this addresses translation risk flagged by macaque biodistribution uncertainty (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution).

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Presence of a reproducible, predefined single-cell transcriptional module shift in microglia ex vivo that correlates with orthogonal intact-EV exposure (spike-in recovery + capture-positive particle co-localization + detergent/protease sensitivity).
candidate_quality_attributes.name: Mechanism-linked potency: intact-EV–predictive ex vivo microglial single-cell transcriptional signature
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: Single-cell microglial transcriptional modulation after orthogonally verified intact-EV exposure provides a mechanism-relevant, discriminating potency signal that is not reducible to bulk particle counts.
candidate_quality_attributes.uncertainty: High: this is an exploratory potency attribute requiring replication and assay development.

edges.competing_explanation: Observed ex vivo transcriptional changes could be driven by soluble secretome components that reach sampled compartments independently of intact EVs.
edges.missing_experiment: Spike-in–controlled in vivo→ex vivo bridge with membrane-disruption and capture-depleted arms combined with single-cell transcriptomics.
edges.model_or_species: rodent context for ex vivo readout
edges.uncertainty: High: rodent efficacy literature shows functional outcomes but lacks orthogonal intact-EV exposure linkage; inference required to propose single-cell microglial readout as a discriminating PD endpoint.

edges.competing_explanation: Failure to detect intact-EV exposure in larger species may reflect administration route, labeling sensitivity, or species-specific clearance rather than absence of EV-mediated exposure.
edges.missing_experiment: Matched intact-EV verification assay in short-interval in vivo samples concurrent with ex vivo single-cell readout.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: macaque data demonstrate intranasal delivery limitations that heighten the need for orthogonal in vivo verification; competing explanations include formulation/administration differences or labeling artifacts.

nodes.statement: An orthogonally defined intact-EV signature (exogenous spike-in recovery + capture-positive signal that co-localizes with particle-count peaks and is detergent/protease-sensitive) identifies a membrane-protected particle fraction in the administered material.

If orthogonally verified intact-EV exposure is present in short-interval nasal lavage/CSF/olfactory-mucosa samples after intranasal dosing, then ex vivo tissue-resident microglia isolated from treated animals will show a reproducible, specific single-cell transcriptional modulation (distinct cluster-level gene-expression shifts) relative to controls.

If the administered material is capture-depleted or membrane-disrupted prior to dosing, or lacks the spike-in–validated intact-EV signature, then the short-interval ex vivo microglial transcriptional modulation will be absent or qualitatively different, indicating the effect depends on intact EV-associated cargo rather than particle abundance or soluble secretome.

competing_explanations: Soluble secretome components that co-fractionate or survive membrane disruption mediate ex vivo transcriptional changes independent of intact EVs.
Apparent orthogonal in vivo exposure may reflect residual label or spike-in/tracer artifacts rather than native intact-EV delivery.
dependencies: Access to a characterized exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer and validated immuno-capture reagents
Short-interval in vivo sampling approvals and operational setup
design_question: Daily question: Does orthogonally verified in vivo exposure of a spike-in–validated, membrane-protected intact-EV fraction after intranasal dosing causally produce a reproducible short-interval ex vivo microglial transcriptional signature that is lost when the same material is membrane-disrupted or capture-depleted?
expected_measurable_effect: If the hypothesis is supported: short-interval (predefined brief post-dose window) ex vivo single-cell RNA-seq of microglia-like cells from olfactory-bulb–adjacent tissue will show a reproducible transcriptional signature (cluster shift and differential expression of predefined inflammatory/regenerative gene modules) that correlates with orthogonal in vivo evidence of intact-EV exposure (presence of capture-positive spike-in-validated signal and particle co-localization). This signature will be absent or qualitatively altered in capture-depleted or detergent/protease-treated arms (falsification outcome).

experiment.assay: Integrated orthogonal in vivo→ex vivo workflow: (A) pre-dose in vitro characterization of all arms with density/size fractionation, particle counts per fraction, immuno-capture readouts for endogenous markers and spike-in tracer, and detergent/protease protection testing; (B) intranasal administration (randomized animals) with a predefined short post-dose interval optimized to maximize recoverable signal; (C) collect nasal lavage, CSF (if feasible), and olfactory-bulb–adjacent tissue; (D) orthogonally verify intact-EV exposure in collected fluids/tissue (capture + particle counts + spike-in recovery); (E) isolate tissue microglia (acutely) and perform single-cell RNA-seq; (F) analyze for predefined transcriptional modules (inflammatory and regenerative gene sets) and cluster shifts comparing arms; (G) correlate presence/absence and reproducibility of microglial single-cell signature with orthogonal in vivo exposure evidence.
experiment.comparator: Four-arm in vivo design (same conditioned-medium lot; all arms spiked identically with exogenous tracer prior to fractionation where applicable): (1) intact-EV–enriched preparation (capture-positive bounded fraction), (2) secretome-retaining concentrated conditioned medium, (3) intact-EV–enriched preparation treated with detergent + protease (membrane-disrupted) prior to administration, (4) particle-count–matched but capture-depleted preparation (if achievable).
experiment.control: Positive assay controls: characterized small EVs and dexamethasone in ex vivo microglial assay; negative controls: vehicle-only and buffer fractions; internal recovery control: exogenous spike-in per sample; capture-compatibility and spike-in controls to exclude assay interference.
dependencies: Availability of an orthogonally labeled intact-EV spike-in tracer and validated capture reagents
Operational single-cell RNA-seq capacity and bioinformatics pipeline for microglial module analysis
Animal protocol approvals for short-interval tissue/fluid collection
experiment.failure_criterion: No reproducible linkage between orthogonal in vivo intact-EV verification and the ex vivo microglial single-cell signature across replicates (i.e., capture-positive verification does not predict the transcriptional outcome), or particle-count–matched capture-negative or membrane-disrupted arms produce equivalent single-cell signatures, indicating the effect is not intact-EV–dependent.
experiment.falsification_outcome: If failure criteria are met (with validated spike-in recovery and capture-compatibility controls), the hypothesis is falsified: short-interval microglial transcriptional modulation is not dependent on intact-EV exposure for this preparation and route. The program must treat the material as functionally indistinguishable from secretome for short-interval PD and redirect potency/CMC strategy accordingly.
experiment.hypothesis_tested: An orthogonally verified, membrane-protected intact-EV fraction (spike-in validated, capture-positive, particle-peak co-localized, detergent/protease-sensitive) is necessary for a reproducible short-interval ex vivo microglial transcriptional modulation following intranasal dosing; particle-count-matched capture-depleted or membrane-disrupted material will not produce the same transcriptional signature.
experiment.primary_readout: Qualitative, reproducible presence (yes/no across replicates) of a predefined microglial single-cell transcriptional signature (cluster-level differential expression of inflammatory/regenerative modules) in animals dosed with capture-positive, spike-in–validated intact-EV material that correlates with orthogonal evidence of intact-EV exposure (capture-positive signal co-localized with particle peaks and spike-in recovery) and is absent or qualitatively altered in membrane-disrupted or capture-depleted arms.
experiment.question: Does orthogonally verified intact-EV exposure (spike-in recovery + capture-positive particle co-localization + detergent/protease sensitivity) after intranasal dosing produce a reproducible short-interval ex vivo microglial single-cell transcriptional modulation that is lost when the same material is membrane-disrupted or capture-depleted?
required_material: MSC-conditioned medium from a single characterized source-cell lot processed into: (A) bounded intact-EV–enriched fraction (e.g., program-defined SEC/iodixanol-bounded) and (B) concentrated conditioned medium (secretome-retaining) from same lot
Exogenous characterized intact-EV spike-in tracer (orthogonal species or isotope-labeled) to add pre-fractionation for recovery controls
Immuno-capture reagents for canonical EV surface markers (anti-CD63/CD9/CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5) and validated capture-compatibility buffers
Particle counter (NTA or TRPS) and reagents
Detergent (Triton X-100 or equivalent), protease (proteinase K), and RNase reagents for membrane-disruption/protection controls
Density-gradient materials (iodixanol) or SEC fractionation setup and fraction collectors

Animal model: rodents suitable for short-interval intranasal dosing and rapid tissue harvest (approved protocol), with capacity for collecting nasal lavage, CSF (if feasible), and olfactory-bulb–adjacent tissue
Single-cell RNA-seq pipeline reagents and instrumentation for microglia isolation (enzymatic tissue dissociation, microglia enrichment), library prep, sequencing, and downstream analysis pipelines
Controls: characterized small-EV positive control material; vehicle-only and buffer-only negative controls; dexamethasone or known anti-inflammatory control for assay validation
secondary_readouts: Spike-in tracer recovery percentage and membrane-protection behavior in lavage/CSF/tissue capture fractions (qualitative: recovered & detergent-sensitive vs not recovered)
Co-localization metrics between particle-count peaks and capture-positive ELISA signal in both administered material and recovered lavage/CSF fractions
Protein:particle ratios of administered materials and of captured fractions

Single-cell metrics: proportion of microglia in altered transcriptional clusters, differential expression of predefined gene modules, and reproducibility across biological replicates (n >= 3 animals per arm, multiple independent conditioned-medium preps if feasible)
experiment.success_criterion: Qualitative success: across independent replicates (n >= 3 animals per arm and >= 3 conditioned-medium preps where feasible), only animals dosed with spike-in–validated, capture-positive intact-EV material reproducibly show the predefined microglial single-cell transcriptional signature; this signature is abolished or absent in membrane-disrupted or capture-depleted arms, and orthogonal in vivo exposure metrics (spike-in recovery + capture co-localized with particle peaks) are concordant with the presence/absence of the signature.

explicit_inferences: Inference: Rodent intranasal efficacy signals motivate an in vivo→ex vivo bridge but do not establish intact-EV exposure; orthogonal spike-in and membrane-protection controls are required to attribute ex vivo transcriptional modulation to intact EVs (labeling and assay controls per MISEV2023).

Inference: A single-cell transcriptional readout in tissue-resident microglia increases mechanistic resolution relative to bulk cytokine assays and can discriminate subtle, EV-dependent PD signals from soluble-secretome effects.
falsification_criteria: Validated spike-in recovery in capture-positive fractions is observed but no reproducible microglial single-cell transcriptional signature is detected across independent biological replicates (n >= 3), implying intact-EV exposure does not produce the proposed short-interval ex vivo effect.

Particle-count–matched capture-depleted or detergent/protease-disrupted arms produce equivalent microglial transcriptional responses to capture-positive arms, indicating the effect is not dependent on intact EV capture/protection.
human_decisions_required: Select single-cell microglial transcriptional modules / gene sets to predefine as the primary mechanistic readout
Approve source-cell lot and production parity for the bounded vs secretome preparations
Approve animal numbers, short-interval timing, and ethical protocols
manufacturability_assessment: Requires production of matched bounded (capture-positive) and secretome-retaining preparations from the same source-cell lot, plus a characterized exogenous intact-EV spike-in. Early investment in orthogonal capture reagents, particle counting, and single-cell processing capacity is needed; success would focus CMC on fractionation and process envelopes that preserve membrane protection.
manufacturing_rationale: Requiring a spike-in–validated, membrane-protected fraction as the drug-substance identity gate focuses CMC development on fractionation and process conditions that preserve membrane integrity (reducing downstream assay ambiguity), enabling targeted potency assay development and comparability testing per MISEV guidance.
measurement_strategy: Qualitative orthogonal in vivo verification (spike-in recovery + capture-positive particle co-localization + detergent/protease sensitivity) plus ex vivo single-cell RNA-seq of microglia with predefined module-based readout (presence/absence and reproducibility across replicates). Use spike-in to control assay recovery and include detergent/protease and capture-depleted arms to falsify EV-dependence.
novelty_statement: Novelty: This hypothesis couples per-sample exogenous intact-EV spike-in recovery and orthogonal capture/protection verification in short-interval in vivo samples with an ex vivo single-cell transcriptional readout of tissue-resident microglia. Prior SGL-001 proposals used bulk cytokine or ELISA-based ex vivo readouts; the proposed single-cell microglial transcriptomic bridge provides a higher-resolution, mechanism-relevant PD discriminator that is not present in the cited prior hypotheses and is designed specifically to discriminate intact-EV–associated potency from soluble secretome effects under matched orthogonal exposure controls.
principal_risks: Assay sensitivity: inability to detect orthogonal intact-EV exposure in short-interval lavage/CSF/tissue confounds interpretation.
Spike-in behavior: spike-in tracer may not faithfully reflect endogenous EV behavior in vivo.
Biological relevance: microglial transcriptional changes may be subtle or confounded by tissue harvest stress.
proposed_potency_relationship: If present reproducibly, the single-cell microglial transcriptional signature will serve as a qualitative potency gate predictive of short-interval PD linked to intact-EV exposure; absence across replicates falsifies EV-mediated short-interval PD for this assay.
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: Adopt a mechanism-linked potency gate defined as: a spike-in–validated, membrane-protected intact-EV fraction (capture-positive, particle-peak co-localized, detergent/protease-sensitive) that predicts a reproducible short-interval ex vivo microglial transcriptional modulation after intranasal administration; use as a qualitative potency-linked product-identity attribute (non-numeric).
title: Hypothesis: A spike-in–validated, membrane-protected intact-EV fraction predicts a reproducible short-interval ex vivo microglial transcriptional modulation after intranasal dosing (single-cell readout)
